title: Can Sovereign Citizen's really travel without a driver's license?
summary: Short explainer that the constitutional right to travel concerns crossing state lines, not cars, and that licensing and taxes still apply.

assertions.quote: so there is a right to travel but it has nothing to do with cars
you have to be licensed to drive that's just the truth
if they tell you not to pay your taxes you will end up like Wesley Snipes in jail owing 19 million dollars

verdicts.note: Filing is mandatory under IRC 6012; non-filers face civil and criminal penalties, and circuits upheld failure-to-file convictions of people arguing filing is voluntary; the document covers tax-protester grounds generally, including sovereign/state-citizen arguments.
After the 'natural person' argument failed in court, criminal prosecution of Paradigm students and educators continued for years; several gurus were convicted of failing to file.
A Detaxer was convicted of failing to file returns for 1995-97, and Canadian courts hold that wrong tax theories are no mistake-of-law defence.
An Australian appellant convicted of failing to file tax returns for three years failed with Magna Carta arguments.
FBI cites a sovereign-citizen couple convicted of federal income tax evasion and lists tax violations among the movement's typical offenses; anecdotal, not a rate.
